frame.rotation: The whole monument is rotated about +Y so the north face points west of true north by the chosen azimuth. Feature coordinates in this file are in the pyramid frame, before that rotation.

disagreements.chosen: 230.36375 m, the mean of Cole's four sides
disagreements.range: 230.253 m (Cole north) to 230.454 m (Cole south); Petrie mean 230.348 m; Dash 2015 mean about 230.353 m (755 ft 9 in)
disagreements.why: Cole 1925 measured the casing foot with invar wires. Petrie's 1883 mean and Dash's 2015 mean sit 11–16 mm away, inside the corner-socket uncertainty Petrie himself discussed.

disagreements.chosen: 51°52′00″ (Petrie's measured casing angle) applied to Cole's mean base, giving 146.721 m
disagreements.range: Petrie 51°52′ ± 2′. The seked of 5½ palms is atan(14/11) = 51°50′34″, inside that tolerance. Petrie's own height, from his base and this angle, is 5,776 ± 7 inches (146.710 m).
disagreements.why: The mesh has to be one triangle. Using the measured angle on the chosen base keeps the slope and the height consistent. The 11 mm gap with Petrie's height is smaller than his ±7 inch tolerance.

disagreements.chosen: 3′06.25″ west of true north, the mean of Cole's four side deviations
disagreements.range: Cole's sides differ among themselves from 1′57″ to 5′30″. Petrie's casing mean is −3′43″.
disagreements.why: Cole's azimuths are tied to the same casing-foot lines as the chosen base. The sides are not parallel, so a single rotation is a mean.

disagreements.range: 138.5–139 m. Procureur et al. 2023 say the pyramid is 139 m high today.
disagreements.why: 139 m is a rounded statement in the muon paper. 138.5 m is the figure used for the truncated core, at the bottom of that rounding.

disagreements.chosen: 5.229 m north–south and 5.752 m east–west (Petrie 205.85 by 226.47 inches)
disagreements.range: Many secondary accounts, including Wikipedia, swap the two axes.
disagreements.why: Petrie's wall-by-wall table measures 205.85 inches from north wall to south wall and 226.47 inches from west wall to east wall. He also notes that this north–south width matches the King's Chamber.

disagreements.chosen: Horizontal void, 30 m long, Grand Gallery cross-section, centred 20 m north of the pyramid centre with its floor set so the centre is 45 m from the Queen's Chamber
disagreements.range: Length is a minimum. The 2017 paper leaves the void horizontal or inclined, and possibly several adjacent spaces. No centreline coordinates were published.
disagreements.why: The horizontal hypothesis is one of the two drawn in Procureur et al. 2023, figure 1. The placement satisfies the constraints that were published: above the gallery, at least 30 m, similar cross-section, 40–50 m from the Queen's Chamber.

summaries.original-casing: The finished pyramid was a casing of fine Tura limestone over a core of local stone. Almost all of that casing is gone. What is drawn is the original shell: Cole's mean base and Petrie's measured face angle.
summaries.core-masonry: The monument as it stands is the stepped core, truncated where the casing and the capstone were removed. The mesh uses the mean plane of Petrie's core and a standing height of 138.5 m. The steps are a visual envelope, not the two hundred surveyed courses.
summaries.casing-remnant-north: Cole found the original casing still in place along 20 m of the north side, on the pavement. The length is his. The height of the block drawn here is only a stand-in for the lowest course.
summaries.pavement: The builders levelled a pavement and set the casing on it, leaving a margin of about 40 cm. Cole found that margin 38 cm wide on the west, 42 cm on the north and 48 cm on the east. The pavement is treated as flat. A rock knoll inside the masonry is not modelled.
summaries.descending-passage: The original doorway is on the north face, 7.29 m east of the centre and 16.97 m above the pavement. From there a passage 1.06 m wide and 1.20 m high descends south at 26°31′23″, through the masonry and into the bedrock, to a point about 30 m below the pavement.
summaries.subterranean-passage: A low horizontal passage leaves the foot of the descending passage and runs south into the unfinished chamber. It is rock-cut and irregular; the box is Petrie's mean section.
summaries.subterranean-chamber: The Subterranean Chamber, or Pit, is cut in the bedrock and was never finished. The roof is the most regular surface. The floor is quarry-trenched, and at the west end it rises to within about 25 cm of the roof. The volume drawn uses the eastern floor, 140 inches below the roof.
summaries.subterranean-south-passage: A rough dead-end drift continues south from the chamber. Petrie read it as a first working passage, meant to be enlarged. The box is the mean of a winding cut.
summaries.ascending-passage: Where the floor of the descending passage is 1,110.64 inches from the original doorway, the ascending passage branches upward to the south. Three granite plugs still close its lower end. The upper end is the threshold of the Grand Gallery, 21.66 m above the pavement.
summaries.granite-plugs: Three (originally more) granite blocks were slid down the ascending passage to seal it. They are narrower at the bottom, 38.2 inches, so they wedge in the contracted mouth. Al-Ma'mun's workmen could not shift them and tunnelled around them through the softer limestone.
summaries.queens-passage: From the foot of the Grand Gallery a horizontal passage runs south to the Queen's Chamber. Near the chamber the floor drops by about half a metre, so the last stretch is taller. The passage axis stays about 7.29 m east of the pyramid's centre.
summaries.queens-chamber: The Queen's Chamber sits on the pyramid's north–south centreline. Petrie measured it 205.85 inches north to south and 226.47 inches east to west, with a gabled roof whose ridge is 245.1 inches above the unfinished floor. The east–west position drawn here assumes the passage meets the middle of the north wall.
summaries.queens-niche: A corbelled niche in the east wall, 41 inches deep. It narrows in four overlaps from about 62 inches at the floor to 20 inches at the top. Its centre sits about 25 inches off the chamber's midline.
summaries.queens-north-shaft: The north shaft leaves the chamber horizontally for 76 inches, then rises at 37°28′. Petrie projected that slope to the casing and did not find an outer mouth. Later robots found a blocking stone. The line drawn is his straight projection, not the bent shaft that was explored.
summaries.queens-south-shaft: The south shaft is the pair of the north one: 80 inches horizontal, then 38°28′ upward. The line is Petrie's projection to the south face. The explored shaft stops at a blocking stone short of the casing.
summaries.grand-gallery: The Grand Gallery continues the ascending passage at the same easting: 2.09 m wide at the walls, 1.04 m wide at the ceiling, and about 8.6 m high vertically, corbelled in seven laps. The floor drawn is Petrie's virtual floor, from the gallery door to the south wall.
summaries.antechamber: A granite room between the Grand Gallery and the King's Chamber, 116.3 by 65.0 inches in plan and 149 inches high. Slots in the walls once held portcullis slabs. The leaf that remains is a raised pair of stones, not a door that still slides.
summaries.kings-north-passage: The short low passage from the south wall of the Grand Gallery into the Antechamber. The length is Petrie's, 52 inches from that wall to the north end of the Antechamber. The height is reconstructed.
summaries.kings-south-passage: The low passage from the Antechamber to the King's Chamber, 100.8 inches on Petrie's floor distances. The height is reconstructed at the same section as the passage north of the Antechamber.
summaries.kings-chamber: A granite room 10.48 m east–west and 5.24 m north–south. The floor sits 42.99 m above the pavement and the ceiling 48.84 m, both uneven by a couple of inches. The walls have opened slightly along the joints; Petrie corrected the original lengths by a few tenths of an inch. The sarcophagus is not drawn.
summaries.kings-north-shaft: Petrie measured the northern shaft from its outer end: the portions he could see average 31°33′, and he thought the whole shaft was probably not steeper than 31°. The mouth height inside the chamber is reconstructed at 0.91 m. The shaft is drawn straight, at the measured outer angle, to the casing.
summaries.kings-south-shaft: The southern shaft's measured portions average 45°13′40″ and steepen toward the outside. It is drawn straight at that mean angle. The real channel is not perfectly straight: Petrie saw it curve by more than its own width.
summaries.relieving-chambers: Five compartments sit on the King's Chamber ceiling: Davison's, Wellington's, Nelson's, Lady Arbuthnot's and Campbell's. Petrie, quoting Vyse, puts their apex near 2,525 inches above the pavement. The five voids are spaced evenly under that apex. Their individual heights are not Vyse's measured heights.
summaries.well-shaft: An irregular shaft from the west side of the Grand Gallery floor, 35.4 inches south of the gallery's north wall, down to the descending passage. It was the way out for the workers who released the plugs. Only the mouth is fixed by Petrie. The path drawn — a drop to a grotto near pavement level, then down to the descending passage — is a schematic of the published section.
summaries.mamun-tunnel: The passage visitors use. Tradition credits the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun, around 820, with forcing it; some scholars think he cleared an older robbers' tunnel. It enters low on the north face and joins the pyramid's passages at the plugs. Both the sill height and the cross-section drawn here are schematic.
summaries.north-face-chevron: A gable of large limestone blocks over the original entrance, now exposed because the casing is gone. The North Face Corridor sits just behind it. The thickness matches the 0.84 m of stone the muon survey found in front of that corridor. The span and the rise are schematic.
summaries.north-face-corridor: ScanPyramids' North Face Corridor, measured in 2023: 9.06 m long, 2.02 m wide and 2.18 m high, horizontal, centred on the chevron and on the descending passage. Its floor is about 20 m above the ground. It is placed 0.84 m behind the casing plane. The paper measures that 0.84 m from the chevron's outer face, which stood slightly behind the lost casing.
summaries.big-void: ScanPyramids' Big Void, published in Nature in 2017. It is at least 30 m long, with a cross-section similar to the Grand Gallery, and it lies above that gallery, 40–50 m from detectors in the Queen's Chamber. The paper does not publish a centreline, and it allows both a horizontal and an inclined void. This model draws the horizontal hypothesis only: 30 m, the gallery's cross-section, 45 m from the Queen's Chamber.
